title: Filtered colimits of etale cohomology on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, meaning that every open cover has a finite subcover and the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Let $D$ be a small filtered category (it is nonempty and every finite diagram admits a cocone) and let $(F_d)_{d\in D}$ be a diagram of abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every $q\ge0$, with cohomology the right derived functors of global sections of abelian sheaves, the canonical map $$\varinjlim_{d\in D}H^q(X,F_d)\longrightarrow H^q\!\left(X,\varinjlim_{d\in D}F_d\right)$$ is an isomorphism. The colimit on the right is in abelian sheaves.

proof.text: Use the enlarged etale site $\mathcal C_X$ of algebraic spaces etale over $X$, with terminal object $X/X$. The scheme-object inclusion gives a restriction equivalence on set sheaves by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density]. It gives an additive equivalence on abelian sheaves too: extend the addition, zero and inverse maps through this fully faithful, finite-product-preserving equivalence; their equations hold because they hold after restriction. Global sections are maps from the terminal set sheaf, endowed with sectionwise addition, so restriction identifies global-section functors. Thus we may transfer the diagram to abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C_X$. Choose the common universe so both sites and their covering sets are small, as in the cited comparison.

source.place: Tags 03G0, 03G1 and 03H7, definition-spaces-etale-site, lemma-compare-etale-sites and remark-explain-equivalence.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B$ be the objects $U\to X$ with $U$ qcqs, and take $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ to consist of all finite coverings of such objects by qcqs objects. Given any covering $\{V_j\to U\}$ with $U\in\mathcal B$, cover each $V_j$ by affine scheme components using [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. The composites of these components with $V_j\to U$ are etale scheme maps by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]; hence their point images in $|U|$ are open by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. They cover $|U|$. Its quasi-compactness selects finitely many components, each still factoring through its original $V_j$. Affine schemes are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and the same scheme-test property holds when they are regarded as representable spaces. These components therefore give a member of $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ refining the original covering. If $U$ is empty take the empty family; its refinements and covering condition are valid.

source.place: Tag 073E, lemma-colimits, proof: cofinal finite coverings; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03FX, 03BX and 03H6.

proof.text: For a member $\{U_a\to U\}$ of $\mathrm{Cov}_0$, the base $U$ and all factors $U_a$ are qcqs. Apply [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-fibre-product] to two factors over $U$, then inductively to the accumulated fibre product and the next factor over the same $U$. This gives every iterated intersection, allowing repetitions, as a qcqs algebraic space. The pullback and composition clauses of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] show that its structural map to $X$ is etale, so it is an object of $\mathcal B$. Thus both hypotheses of the finite-cover criterion hold, including all higher covering intersections, not just pairwise ones.

source.place: Tag 073E, lemma-colimits, proof: permanence by spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 073B.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-site-finite-cover-cohomology-colimit] to $\mathcal C_X$, $\mathcal B$, $\mathrm{Cov}_0$, the given small filtered index $D$, and the transferred diagram. Since the hypothesis on $X$ says precisely that the terminal object $X/X$ lies in $\mathcal B$, its conclusion gives the required isomorphism for evaluation at $X/X$ in every degree $q\geq0$. This is global sections on the enlarged site, with the canonical map induced by the given coprojections.

source.place: Tag 073E, lemma-colimits, final sentence, applying sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0739.

proof.text: Transfer this assertion back through restriction. Both abelian sheaf categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. The additive equivalence and section-functor identification of step 1 satisfy exactly the hypotheses of [lem-exc-equivalence-derived-sections], which gives cohomology identifications natural in each coefficient sheaf. An equivalence preserves the colimit together with its legs: cocones from the restricted diagram to $G$ correspond under its quasi-inverse to cocones from the original diagram to the inverse image of $G$, and the unique factorization property is unchanged. Naturality of the cohomology identifications therefore carries every coprojection map in step 4 to $H^q(F_d\to\varinjlim F)$. The induced map out of the group colimit is consequently the map in the statement by the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Its isomorphism property follows from step 4.

source.place: Tags 03G1 and 03H7, equivalence of etale topoi, applied to injective resolutions and canonical coprojections.

proof_origin.place: Tag 073E, lemma-colimits, with the enlarged-site equivalence of Tags 03G1 and 03H7 made explicit.
